name: Schizachyrium

project_scope.note: The current project pool has one canonical Schizachyrium anchor; species taxonomy/range decisions remain in the species package.

recognition.where_to_look_first: Native little bluestem shows DISTINCT relatively tight bunches and many SHORT silvery racemes terminating separate leafy upper branches. Introduced KR bluestem instead presents several LONG fingerlike racemes gathered into one terminal panicle; both require same-plant leaf collars and paired spikelet macro.
priority: numerous separate SHORT terminal or axillary racemes throughout upper culm
true leaf collar and mature paired spikelets
short terminal fuzzy racemes on branchlets

comparisons.rule: Schizachyrium scatters many short racemes across branched upper stems; Bothriochloa concentrates its rames into a more unified terminal head whose node hair and branch architecture are major ID clues.
Anatherum glomeratum builds a dense brushlike fluffy crown; Schizachyrium scoparium shows repeated short racemes terminating separate upper branchlets.

look_here_first: LITTLE BLUESTEM: upper flowering shoots have separate SHORT silk-haired solitary racemes at MANY leafy branch tips; KR has a few-or-many LONG terminal fingers from one grouped terminal panicle. New official USGS leaf-base photo shows green overlapped sheath and some fine sheath-margin hairs, but this is NOT a ligule measurement. Verify the flattened/keeled actual sheath, TRUE short membranous ligule (FNA 0.5–2 mm; Kew GrassBase 1–3 mm and describes margin as eciliate; some regional descriptions call the margin fringed) with scale, and same-plant paired spikelets. Pedicellate companions differ across little-bluestem varieties, so avoid a tiny-spikelet-only rigid key. See the species updated 16-step source-backed photo course and original DigFlora linked anatomy.

cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.title: Native little bluestem vs invasive KR — flowering & nonflowering field key
cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.memory_rule: A FEW LONG fingers together (KR) versus MANY SHORT fuzzy racemes on SEPARATE upper branches (little bluestem).
quick_split: KR / Bothriochloa ischaemum — introduced Old World bluestem; terminal panicle typically 3–8 or more elongated fingerlike spikelet-bearing branches. Leaf UPPER surface just above collar may have stiff papilla-based hairs. Node hair sources conflict; not a single-character proof.

Little bluestem / Schizachyrium scoparium — Hays native, generally dense persistent bunch; many short racemes arise from different branches in the upper plant and become silvery/fluffy in fruit. Roots/leaf collar and actual spikelet pairs strengthen ID.
field_crew_sequence: Photograph rooted whole clump and top-to-bottom reproductive architecture.
Trace WHERE each raceme originates: all near one terminal center = KR candidate; dispersed short units on many upper culm branches = little bluestem candidate.
At 10×, inspect KR upper leaf surface right above collar for papilla-based hairs; check true ligule on same culm.
Check paired sessile fertile/pedicelled companion spikelet details with 1-mm scale; where unresolved label bluestem sp.
Before removal or seed collection, rule out native cane bluestem and silver bluestem plus introduced Kleberg bluestem.
cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.node_hair_caution: Do not enforce smooth KR nodes: Texas A&M calls songarica nodes hairless; local UT Austin morphological work reports short or appressed hairs. Use combined characters. Cane bluestem tends to bear a pronounced BEARD at nodes.

cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.first_clue: KR bluestem (introduced): look for several long, slender fingerlike flowering branches clustered together at the tip of a stem. Native little bluestem has shorter fuzzy flowering branches along separate upper stems.

expert_collar_and_node_notes.Leaf collar: On a confirmed same-plant specimen, inspect stiff papilla-based hairs on the upper leaf blade near the collar; photograph the true ligule with a ruler.
expert_collar_and_node_notes.Spikelet pairs: At 10–20× magnification, separate an attached sessile fertile spikelet from its pedicelled companion and check the awn; the current photos do not resolve this.
expert_collar_and_node_notes.Node-hair caution: Do NOT use hairless stem nodes as a required test. Texas A&M describes glabrous KR nodes, while local UT Austin treatments have noted short hairs. A heavy beard is useful when considering native cane bluestem.
expert_collar_and_node_notes.Native versus invasive decision: Use multiple characters and preserve the project's nonnative invasive-comparison status; never remove native bluestem on a seedhead silhouette alone.

diagnostic_steps: STEP 1 — LITTLE: look at the annotated photo. Follow a short silky raceme DOWN to its own leafy branch/sheath. Find that same pattern repeated on another branch.
STEP 2 — BEFORE FLUFF: use the yellow-anther photo to recognize little bluestem in flower before dense white seed hairs develop.
STEP 3 — KR: open the next side-by-side photos and trace several LONG fingers that converge into ONE terminal panicle (these photographs show architecture, not collar).

STEP 4 — IF NO FLOWERS: look for sharply keeled/flattened leaf sheath on a tight little-bluestem bunch; examine suspected KR upper blade above collar for long stiff papilla-based hairs; neither is decisive without corroboration.
cross_genus_bluestem_comparison.no_flower_rule: Nonflowering grass: sharply keeled little bluestem sheaths and tidy tuft vs often spreading KR crowns; inspect upper leaf blade for KR papilla-based hairs; NEVER a reliable final ID without further mature structures.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Follow one complete upper culm from the flag leaf to EVERY flowering branch. Inspect the upper blade surface immediately above its ligule.
field_matrix.little_bluestem: Separate SHORT silky racemes end many leafy lateral branches, usually one unit per sheath. The sheath may be sharply keeled; the blade usually lacks long stiff papillose hairs near its collar.
field_matrix.look_alike: KR makes several much LONGER narrow fingers in a terminal cluster, generally 3–8 in Texas A&M; up to 17 in complex regional flora. KR often has scattered long stiff papilla-based hairs immediately above collar.
field_matrix.no_seedhead: A tight perennial base + keeled sheath favors little, spreading/kinked stems + papilla-based collar hairs favors KR; take more than one leaf and do not treat habit as a final answer.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Several long fingers all connected near ONE central panicle = KR candidate; numerous separate short racemes on leafy side branches = native LITTLE candidate. Under uncertainty preserve the plant.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Count the relatively stout exposed flowering fingers and inspect their common attachment point.
field_matrix.little_bluestem: Many short individual racemes at distinct upper leafy branch tips.
field_matrix.look_alike: Big has a few comparatively stout exposed turkey-foot-like racemes clustered together (commonly 2–6); inspect complete tip and spikelets.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Few stout fingers at one tip = BIG; numerous separate short fluffy plumes along upper shoots = LITTLE.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Inspect entire silhouette; part the cottony head to see hidden short paired racemes and their spathe-like bracts.
field_matrix.little_bluestem: Multiple individual short racemes arise from spaced leafy upper branches rather than one compact brush.
field_matrix.look_alike: Bushy has a densely crowded, often broad oblong cottony crown with many short paired rames packed together, commonly at moist sites.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Big broad dense brush = BUSHY candidate; distinct separated short upper branch tips = LITTLE candidate.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Inspect how paired rames sit inside and emerge from long, flattened spathe-like sheaths.
field_matrix.little_bluestem: Generally single short raceme per upper leafy branch/sheath; distinguish in several units.
field_matrix.look_alike: Broomsedge usually holds paired hairy rames partly within more conspicuous longer flattened spathes; narrow upper flowering outline.
field_matrix.quick_rule: One short raceme per upper leafy branch favors LITTLE; paired sheath-held flowering units favor BROOMSEDGE.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Inspect two true culm nodes just above the leaf sheath and the complete silver inflorescence.
field_matrix.little_bluestem: Short individual branch-end racemes; tight bunch without a distinctive ring of long silky hairs around every true node.
field_matrix.look_alike: Cane has a conspicuous long soft white beard at stem nodes and broad multi-branched fanlike seedhead.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Heavy true node beard + broad fan = CANE; separate short silky upper branchlets = LITTLE.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Trace whether flowering units make a narrow contracted cottony head or independent upper leafy branches.
field_matrix.little_bluestem: Upper leafy branches each carry an individual short silky raceme, not a singular narrow cotton column.
field_matrix.look_alike: Silver is a compact narrow white-silky plume with numerous SHORT crowded branches and usually smooth pale nodes.
field_matrix.quick_rule: One narrow cottony panicle with many crowded short rames = SILVER candidate; distributed separate racemes = LITTLE.

field_matrix.where_to_look: Check mature terminal raceme-group arrangement, true nodes, ligule and complete reproductive structure.
field_matrix.little_bluestem: Different leafy upper branch origins with individual shorter racemes and characteristic keeled sheaths.
field_matrix.look_alike: Introduced Kleberg can mimic the terminal fingerlike KR bluestem silhouette; swollen or whitish node/raceme details require regional key.
field_matrix.quick_rule: Do not call every fingered nonnative-looking grass KR or confuse it with native little without attached full head and collar.

visual_comparison.title: LITTLE vs KR — live photo comparison with flowering and seed-stage views
visual_comparison.subtitle: See short separated little-bluestem racemes beside Texas KR's longer grouped terminal fingers. Early flowering anthers and later silky seed are separate stages. Seven new original Bob Harms local true Schizachyrium photos now physically backed by canonical species JPEGs: North Hays bunch, branching, flowers, attached and isolated units and true collar/sheath. Microscopy 1mm exact membrane/paired voucher remains.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: KR = several LONG terminal fingers together; LITTLE = SHORT silky racemes arising separately among upper leafy branches.
